findings.reason: The protected source is already an expert-quality backtracking solution. It commits assignments reversibly, uses a set for the reverse bijection, follows established values without branching, and reserves a safe minimum suffix before trying a new nonempty substring. Its structure and naming are clear, so no candidate is justified.

Metadata consistently identifies Premium LeetCode problem 291 and its Python pattern-and-target boolean contract. The Reference preserves the nonempty-substring bijection, all three source examples in order, explanations for the first two examples only, and both source constraints.

The immutable native source remains tied to verified submission 2064317907. It and the app-local source have identical assignment and used-substring state, base cases, mapped-prefix transition, suffix lower bound, candidate range, reversible branch updates, and initial search state; only the required wrapper and type syntax differ.

The former 12/24/48-character tiers exceeded the source maximum of 20. Legal 4/8/20-character repeated-symbol failures now span 5x and grow the pattern through six occurrences, so a correct implementation that validates consistency only after generating complete partitions must explore the intended combinatorial path. The current source passes at -0.02 relative exponent and 1.01x largest ratio; that delayed-consistency control passes every output but fails only scaling at +4.09 and 702.23x.

The manifest now includes the linear substring-work factor in the exponential bound. The Approach defines target length n and pattern length p, derives the boundary-subset search, accounts for live substring storage and recursion, explains reversible assignments and the safe suffix bound, and covers bijection, nonempty, and exact-exhaustion traps.

The hash-bound Premium Reference remains verified against authenticated source evidence, preserving all three examples and their explanation presence, both constraints, the complete bijection semantics, and the zero-visual structure.

coverage: All three authenticated source examples appear first, in source order, with their exact pattern, target, and boolean result.
The two previously hidden correctness rows are now visible trials, and every row uses source-legal nonempty lowercase strings.
The suite covers minimum and maximum pattern and target lengths, one symbol consuming the whole target, equal one-character assignments, and a pattern longer than the target.
Forward-map consistency and reverse-map injectivity are checked separately through repeated-symbol mismatches and distinct symbols attempting to share one substring.
Successful and failing repeated multi-character assignments, extra target suffixes, exact simultaneous exhaustion, and distinct one-character assignments exercise the material backtracking endpoints.

Each expected result was independently derived by enumerating every complete nonempty partition and checking the resulting bijection; the protected source matched this oracle on 15,748 exhaustive small pattern/string pairs.
All 15 correctness cases are visible; the unchanged legal 4-, 8-, and 20-character repeated-symbol failures remain hidden and performance-only in benchmark.json.
